data.body:
Patchset 2 pushed to change 2601 (commit 89afbe561f26, Change-Id preserved). Patchset 1 had LLM-Review+1 but Verified-1; both approvals were outdated by this upload.

WHY PS1 FAILED CI. make lint was green but tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py was not in my verification set, and it failed on PS1:
  FAILED test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree - AssertionError: active=682 new=1 increased=0 stale=0
  FAILED test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree - Extra items in the right set: 'ci_gate::scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py'
The '# mechanism-ok:' marker admits a mechanism at check_mechanism_delta.py --check only. scripts/_mechanism_delta/detect_ci.py::_detect_gate_scripts names every scripts/check_*.py a ci_gate BY ITS PATH (path.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix() over the check_*.py glob), and the two unit tests assert new=0 and set(baseline) == live REGARDLESS of markers. So no contributor can land a new gate script; only an operator running --lock can.

RESTRUCTURE (no new mechanism). Deleted scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py, reverted the Makefile wiring, and folded the identical detector into the guard that failed - tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py. Detection semantics are byte-for-byte the same (last operand after --bare / cwd when the flag takes none / factory results by return position bound at the caller's name / argument at a parameter position the callee creates one at; -c safe.bareRepository=all and the creating call exempt). No mechanism-ok marker, no baseline edit, no --lock, no --force.

Rejected alternatives: folding the rule into check_wall_clock_asserts.py or check_raw_git_writes.py (avoids a new name but merges unrelated concerns into a script whose whole docstring is a different rule - a design distortion, and check_raw_git_writes.py is already 873 lines); naming the script something outside the check_*.py glob (evades the detector by naming and hides a gate from the ratchet that exists to bound gates).

Verification on the committed tree: pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py -> 31 passed; make lint exit 0; make typecheck 'Success: no issues found in 753 source files'; strict config (safe.bareRepository=explicit) across both fixed files + the oracle -> 28 passed; default config tests/interfaces/lifecycle + both files + oracle -> 557 passed. AC3 mutation re-demonstrated against the restructured guard: reverting line 411 to _git(remote, ...) fails test_no_test_addresses_a_bare_repository_by_discovery with 'tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py:411: bare repository \'remote\' addressed via _git()'; restoring returns 6 passed.

PLAN CURRENCY: the description was edited post-claim to match the restructure, so 'rebar review-plan --status' now reports stale-material (description 7842 -> 7903 chars, text changed). The signed attestation from the claim gate predates the restructure. Flagging for whoever closes this - a fresh review-plan may be wanted first.

Not closing - awaiting merge.
